category: PCB Editor command line, environment and user preferences, tuning and check commands, board properties and file types
description: Everyday OrCAD PCB Editor / Allegro knowledge outside the core layout catalog: command-window commands (funckey, button, scriptmode, set/unset/readonly, write, reopen, uprev), startup options, the env file and allegro.ilinit, library path and licensing environment variables, the User Preferences Editor, delay and phase tuning, Z-Copy, database and constraint checks, drawing- and object-level control properties, and the board-side file types (.brd, .art, .drl, .rpt, .jrl/.log, .tcf, symbol types). Where OrCAD PCB Editor 17.4 moved commands to its Check menu, both paths are given.

tools.name: funckey (command)
tools.description: Binds a keyboard key to a PCB Editor command string for the session, or permanently when placed in the env file. Keys can trigger pop-up menu entries, option changes or command sequences separated by semicolons, which removes most mouse travel during routing and placement.
tools.usage: funckey <key> "<command string>"

parameters.name: <key>
parameters.description: Single key, function key, or " " for the space bar.

tools.example:
funckey " " "pop bbdrill -cursor"   (space bar adds a via while routing)
funckey r iangle 90
funckey d "prepopup; pop dyn_option_select @:@Delete"
tools.notes: Put permanent bindings in %HOME%\pcbenv\env. Related: alias (named shortcuts) and button (mouse-wheel bindings).

tools.name: button (mouse wheel bindings)
tools.description: Binds the middle mouse wheel, combined with Shift, Ctrl or Shift+Ctrl, to commands, for example to step the active or alternate layer or to roam the view.
tools.usage: button <Swheel_up|Swheel_down|Cwheel_up|Cwheel_down|SCwheel_up|SCwheel_down> "<command>"
tools.example:
button Swheel_up subclass -+
button Swheel_down altsubclass -+
button Cwheel_up "roam y -$roamInc"

tools.name: scriptmode (+i / +invisible, +e)
tools.description: Changes how commands and scripts run: scriptmode +i (short for +invisible) suppresses forms while a command sequence plays, and scriptmode +e echoes the commands you perform into the command window so they can be copied into aliases, funckeys or .scr scripts.
tools.usage: scriptmode +invisible | +i | +e
tools.example: alias ec "scriptmode +i; prmed; FORM prmedit display_enhance toggle; FORM prmedit done"
tools.notes: Put 'scriptmode +invisible' as the first line of a recorded .scr file to replay it without flashing dialogs.

tools.name: set / unset / readonly (environment variables from the command window)
tools.description: Sets or clears PCB Editor environment variables (the same ones edited in the User Preferences Editor) for the session; in the env file they become permanent. readonly <variable> added by a site administrator makes a variable uneditable; typing readonly alone lists the protected variables.
tools.usage: set <variable> [<value>] | unset <variable> | readonly [<variable>]
tools.example:
set sigsuppress ERROR WARNING
readonly psmpath

tools.name: write / reopen (command-window file commands)
tools.description: write <name> saves a copy of the open design under a new name while keeping the current file open (unlike File > Save As, which switches to the new file); reopen reloads the same design from disk.
tools.usage: write <design_name> | reopen
tools.example:
write board_before_ripup
# ... experiment ...
reopen

tools.name: uprev / uprev_overwrite (library database upgrade)
tools.description: Upgrade symbol, padstack and drawing databases to the current software revision. uprev_overwrite runs from the PCB Editor command window on file patterns; the stand-alone uprev program in a command prompt offers more options (uprev -help).
tools.usage:
uprev_overwrite <pattern>   (e.g. *.dra, *.psm, *.ssm)
uprev -help
tools.example: uprev_overwrite *.dra
tools.notes: Back up the library first: upgraded files cannot be opened by older releases.

tools.name: allegro -safe / -noopengl (startup options)
tools.description: -safe starts the editor without user customisations: the local env file, CDS_SITE configuration, user SKILL code, pre-registered scripts, the ini file of window positions, MRU lists and .geo files. -noopengl disables OpenGL-based enhanced graphics, useful with remote desktops or graphics driver problems.
tools.usage: allegro -safe -noopengl  (also on other Allegro-family executables)
tools.example: Create a desktop shortcut: "<install>\tools\bin\allegro.exe" -safe -noopengl
tools.notes: If a problem disappears with -safe, bisect your env file, SKILL autoloads and site settings.

tools.name: env file (%HOME%\pcbenv\env)
tools.description: Per-user PCB Editor environment file read at startup, holding set commands for variables, alias, funckey and button definitions, and readonly locks. The User Preferences Editor writes to it; site-wide defaults can come from the CDS_SITE hierarchy.
tools.usage: %HOME%\pcbenv\env (plain text: set ..., alias ..., funckey ..., button ..., readonly ...)
tools.example:
set psmpath . D:/lib/symbols $psmpath
funckey r iangle 90
set sigsuppress ERROR WARNING
tools.notes: HOME must be defined (Cadence installs set it); a broken line in env can silently disable later settings.

tools.name: allegro.ilinit (SKILL startup file)
tools.description: SKILL file executed when PCB Editor starts, conventionally placed in %HOME%\pcbenv (or a site directory); it loads custom .il/.ile programs so their axlCmdRegister commands are available in every session.
tools.usage: %HOME%\pcbenv\allegro.ilinit containing load("<file>.il") calls
tools.example:
load("D:/skill/comp_loc.il")
load("D:/skill/my_reports.ile")
tools.notes: Starting with -safe skips user SKILL code, which is the quickest test when a SKILL add-on breaks startup.

tools.name: PSMPATH / PADPATH / STEPPATH (library search paths)
tools.description: Search paths for footprint and mechanical symbols (psmpath), padstacks (padpath) and STEP 3D models (steppath), used when placing parts, refreshing symbols and building the 3D view. They are set under Setup > User Preferences > Paths > Library or with set in the env file.
tools.usage: set psmpath <dir> <dir> ... | set padpath ... | set steppath ...
tools.example:
set psmpath . D:/company/pcb/symbols $psmpath
set padpath . D:/company/pcb/padstacks $padpath
tools.notes: Symbols missing from psmpath cause 'symbol not found' errors during File > Import > Logic. Administrators often mark these paths readonly.

tools.name: HOME / CDSROOT / CDS_SITE (Cadence environment variables)
tools.description: HOME locates the user's Cadence setup (pcbenv for PCB Editor, cdssetup for Capture); CDSROOT points to the SPB installation root (tools\bin, share\pcb and so on); CDS_SITE points to a shared site configuration directory whose settings apply to all users before their personal ones.
tools.usage: Windows environment variables: HOME=<dir>, CDSROOT=C:\Cadence\SPB_<release>, CDS_SITE=<shared dir>
tools.example: CDS_SITE=\\server\cadence_site so every designer shares the same env defaults and drill legend templates.
tools.notes: Programs started with -safe ignore CDS_SITE data. Scripts in the Capture Tcl app note use CDS_INST_DIR for the install root; check which name your release defines.

tools.name: CDS_LIC_FILE / LM_LICENSE_FILE (license server variables)
tools.description: Point OrCAD/Allegro tools to the FlexNet license server or license file, typically port@host. CDS_LIC_FILE is the Cadence-specific variable and takes effect for Cadence products; LM_LICENSE_FILE is the generic FlexNet variable shared with other vendors.
tools.usage: CDS_LIC_FILE=5280@<license-server>  (multiple servers separated by ';' on Windows)
tools.example: setx CDS_LIC_FILE 5280@lic01;5280@lic02
tools.notes: A slow or unreachable entry at the front of the list delays every tool start; put the local/primary server first.

tools.name: Setup > User Preferences (User Preferences Editor)
tools.description: Categorised editor for the hundreds of PCB Editor environment variables (display, datatips, paths, routing, file management, drawing, UI and more) with a search box; changes are saved to the env file. Examples include allegro_etch_length (length meter for unconstrained nets), padentry_factor (diff-pair gathering), dfa_pause_level and color_lastgroup.
tools.usage: Setup > User Preferences... > category tree + Search

parameters.name: Paths > Library
parameters.description: psmpath, padpath, steppath and related paths.

tools.example: Setup > User Preferences > Search 'datatip' to find the delay, location and disable variables.

tools.name: Autosave and ADS output directory variables (File_management)
tools.description: User preference variables under File_management: the Autosave group saves the database automatically at intervals, and the ADS-prefixed Output_dir variables create sub-directories for artwork, plots, logs and reports so outputs do not clutter the board directory.
tools.usage: Setup > User Preferences > File_management > Autosave | Output_dir
tools.example: Enable autosave every 15 minutes and set the artwork output directory to .\artwork.

tools.name: Setup > Datatip Customization
tools.description: Chooses which object attributes and properties appear in the hover datatip for each object type, for example showing the FIXED property on symbol instances so fixed parts are recognisable at a glance.
tools.usage: Setup > Datatip Customization > Object Type > enable properties
tools.example: Object Type = Symbol Instance > enable FIXED and ROOM.

tools.name: Display > Color/Visibility (Color dialog)
tools.description: Sets colours and visibility per class/subclass, and per net, bus or differential pair on the Nets tab, with Visibility controls for quickly enabling or disabling layers. 'Hide Custom Colors' on the Nets tab reverts net colour overrides to layer-based colouring.
tools.usage: Display > Color/Visibility (Options pane colour swatches toggle layers during commands)
tools.example: Nets tab > Hide Custom Colors on an inherited board whose net colours are confusing.

tools.name: Route > Delay Tune
tools.description: Interactively lengthens a net or differential pair that is below its length/delay constraint by drawing accordion, trombone or sawtooth serpentines, with real-time green/red feedback bars against the constraint. Options set gap (e.g. 1x width, 5x space), corner type (90, 45, FullArc), miter size, centring and whether DRC violations are allowed.
tools.usage: Route > Delay Tune; Options pane: Style, Centered, Gap, Corners, Miter size, Allow DRCs

parameters.name: Gap
parameters.description: Edge-to-edge spacing, e.g. '3x width' or '2x space' or a value.

tools.example: Set a Relative Propagation Delay match group in Constraint Manager, then Route > Delay Tune on the short members until their bars turn green.
tools.notes: Available in OrCAD PCB Designer Professional and Allegro PCB Designer tiers that include delay tuning.

tools.name: Route > Phase Tune
tools.description: Adds precise, parameterised phase-compensation bumps (line or arc style) on a differential pair member with single clicks, showing the length added per bump, to fix static or dynamic phase mismatch along the pair.
tools.usage: Route > Phase Tune; Options: Bump Style (Line/Arc), Bump Length, Bump Height, Length added per bump

parameters.name: Bump Length / Height
parameters.description: Default two times the minimum line width from the physical CSet.

tools.example: Click three times near the pin escape of the shorter USB_D member to add three arc bumps.

tools.name: Auto-interactive Phase Tune (AiPT) and Timing Vision
tools.description: High-speed option features on the Route menu: AiPT (with AiDT for delay) automatically adds the length needed to meet phase or match-group constraints on selected pairs and groups, and Timing Vision colours clines on the canvas according to whether they meet their timing constraints.
tools.usage: Route > Auto-interactive Phase Tune (and Auto-interactive Delay Tune); Timing Vision from the Route menu / toolbar
tools.example: Window-select a DDR byte lane, run Auto-interactive Delay Tune, then check with Timing Vision that every trace turns to the pass colour.
tools.notes: Requires Allegro PCB Designer with the High Speed option or an equivalent OrCAD X tier.

tools.name: Z-Copy (Edit > Z-Copy / Shape > Z-Copy)
tools.description: Copies a shape or outline to another class/subclass, optionally contracted or expanded by an offset, and to several layers at once using a wildcard in the target subclass. The classic use is deriving a Route Keepin from the board outline.
tools.usage: Edit > Z-Copy (Allegro) | Shape > Z-Copy (OrCAD PCB Editor); Options: Class, Subclass, Contract/Expand, Offset
tools.example: Class ROUTE KEEPIN, Subclass ALL, Contract 0.5 mm, pick the board outline.

tools.name: Tools > Database Check (Check > Database Check) and Performance Advisor
tools.description: Runs database integrity checks on the open board (the interactive counterpart of dbdoctor) and, through Performance Advisor, suggests settings to improve database and display performance, such as adding VOLTAGE properties to large power nets so they are not scheduled as min-tree.
tools.usage: Tools > Database Check (Allegro) | Check > Database Check (OrCAD PCB Editor 17.4) > options | Performance Advisor
tools.example: Check > Database Check > Update all DRC, Check shape outlines > Check; then Performance Advisor.

tools.name: Display > Constraint (Check > Constraints)
tools.description: Reports how constraints resolve for picked objects: select one element for its physical rules, or window-select two elements for the spacing rule between them together with the measured gap.
tools.usage: Display > Constraint (Allegro) | Check > Constraints (OrCAD PCB Editor 17.4), then select object(s)
tools.example: Window-select both clines of a differential pair to see the applied spacing CSet and actual gap.

tools.name: Display > Property (Check > Properties)
tools.description: Shows property values of elements and, on its Graphics tab, can write chosen property names/values into the canvas as text on Manufacturing/Properties subclass for documentation.
tools.usage: Display > Property (Allegro) | Check > Properties (OrCAD PCB Editor 17.4) > Graphics tab > choose properties > Create
tools.example: Annotate every part with its ROOM value on the Manufacturing/Properties subclass for a placement review plot.

tools.name: Analyze > Model Assignment (Xnets)
tools.description: Assigns signal-integrity (ESpice) models to discrete components; Auto Setup applies default models so series resistors and capacitors join nets into Xnets that Constraint Manager can constrain end to end. With a Constraint Manager-enabled schematic flow Xnets are created automatically.
tools.usage: Analyze > Model Assignment > resolve warnings > Auto Setup
tools.example: Assign models to series termination resistors so DDR address nets are length-matched from driver to receiver as Xnets.
tools.notes: Prevent an Xnet through a specific part with the no_xnet_connection component property. The Xnet name defaults to the alphanumerically lowest member net.

tools.name: nodrc_same_sym_pin / BBVIA_SEPARATION (drawing-level DRC properties)
tools.description: Properties that tune DRC reporting: nodrc_same_sym_pin suppresses pin-to-pin spacing errors within the same symbol (on a symbol, or on the drawing for all symbols); BBVIA_SEPARATION on the drawing suppresses buried/blind via gap DRCs when the vias are separated by at least the given number of layers.
tools.usage: Edit > Properties (Allegro) | Edit > Object Properties (OrCAD) > Find by Name: Drawing > add property
tools.example: Drawing property BBVIA_SEPARATION=2 so stacked microvias two layers apart no longer flag bbvia gap DRCs.

tools.name: void_same_net / no_xnet_connection / FIXED / LOCKED (object properties)
tools.description: Frequently used object properties: void_same_net on a cline makes a same-net plane void around it (e.g. a GND sense line through a GND plane); no_xnet_connection stops Xnet formation through a component; FIXED prevents moving placed objects; LOCKED protects replicate circuits or symbol contents from editing or deletion.
tools.usage: Edit > Properties / Edit > Object Properties > select object > add property; right-click > Fix/Unfix, Unfix All
tools.example: Add void_same_net to the Kelvin GND sense trace; right-click the connector > Fix before autoplacement.

tools.name: Library Drill Report and drill legend template (.dlt)
tools.description: Library Drill Report lists library padstacks with their hole sizes, useful to rationalise drills; the drill legend layout is controlled by .dlt template files (e.g. default-units.dlt under %CDSROOT%\share\pcb\text\nclegend) whose ColumnDefinitions can add metric columns.
tools.usage: Manufacture > NC > Drill Customization > Library Drill Report (Allegro) | Manufacture > Customise Drill Table > Library Drill Report (OrCAD); template: %CDSROOT%\share\pcb\text\nclegend\default-units.dlt
tools.example: ?AlternateUnits "millimeters" plus ColumnDefinitions entries Holesize2 'SIZE MM' and Tolerance2 'TOLERANCE MM' for a dual-unit drill chart.

tools.name: OrCAD PCB Editor 17.4 Check menu vs Allegro menu paths
tools.description: OrCAD PCB Editor 17.4 regrouped several Allegro commands: Display > Status becomes Check > Design Status, Display > Property becomes Check > Properties, Display > Constraint becomes Check > Constraints, Tools > Database Check becomes Check > Database Check, Edit > Properties becomes Edit > Object Properties, Edit > Z-Copy becomes Shape > Z-Copy, Setup > Constraints > Constraint Manager becomes Setup > Constraints, Manufacture > Testprep > Parameters becomes Manufacture > Test points > Parameters, and Tools > Utilities > File Manager becomes Tools > More > File Manager.
tools.usage: Reference mapping when following Allegro-based instructions in OrCAD PCB Editor
tools.example: An Allegro tip says 'Display > Status'; in OrCAD PCB Editor 17.4 use Check > Design Status.
tools.notes: OrCAD X Presto uses a different, ribbon-style UI; command-window commands remain the most portable way to reach functions.

tools.name: .brd
tools.description: Binary PCB Editor/Allegro board database containing stackup, padstacks, placed symbols, nets, routing, shapes, constraints and DRC markers. Newer releases can open older boards (upgrading them on save) but not vice versa.
tools.usage: File > Open > *.brd; command-window write/reopen; batch tools extracta and dbdoctor
tools.example: D:\proj\amp\allegro\amp.brd
tools.notes: Use File > Export > Downrev Design (where available) or ask the recipient's release before sharing a board.

tools.name: .art (Gerber artwork files)
tools.description: Photoplot files written by Manufacture > Artwork, one per film (TOP.art, GND.art, SOLDERMASK_TOP.art...), in RS-274X or other device formats set on the General Parameters tab; photoplot.log records warnings for each film.
tools.usage: Manufacture > Artwork > Film Control > Create Artwork -> <film>.art
tools.example: Zip all *.art, the NC drill files and the IPC-D-356 netlist for the fabricator.
tools.notes: Check photoplot.log for undefined line widths and aperture issues before release.

tools.name: .drl and nc_param.txt (NC drill outputs)
tools.description: Excellon-style NC drill files written by Manufacture > NC > NC Drill (one per drill layer pair for blind/buried structures) together with nc_param.txt holding the format, units and zero-suppression settings from NC Parameters, which the fabricator needs to read the drill data.
tools.usage: Manufacture > NC > NC Parameters (writes nc_param.txt); Manufacture > NC > NC Drill -> *.drl
tools.example: amp-1-4.drl (through holes) plus nc_param.txt in the release package.
tools.notes: Keep drill units/format consistent with the Gerber settings; include the drill legend drawing.

tools.name: .rpt (PCB Editor reports)
tools.description: Text reports written by Tools > Reports (or Quick Reports), such as component, placement, net, unconnected pins, DRC and etch length reports; they can be written as CSV-style text for spreadsheets.
tools.usage: Tools > Reports > select report(s) > Generate Report -> <report>.rpt
tools.example: Generate the Unconnected Pins report and ensure it is empty before artwork.

tools.name: .jrl and .log (journal and log files)
tools.description: PCB Editor writes a session journal (allegro.jrl) of commands and messages in the working directory, and command-specific logs such as netrev.lst for logic import and photoplot.log for artwork. They are the first place to look after a crash or failed import.
tools.usage: Working directory: allegro.jrl, netrev.lst, photoplot.log, <command>.log
tools.example: After File > Import > Logic fails, open netrev.lst and search for ERROR.

tools.name: .tcf (technology file)
tools.description: Technology file capturing a board's cross-section, constraints and related setup so it can be applied to new or existing designs, keeping stackups and rule sets consistent across a product family.
tools.usage: File > Export > Technology File (Techfile in older releases); File > Import > Technology File
tools.example: Export 8L_HDI.tcf from a proven board and import it into the next derivative before routing.
tools.notes: Importing overwrites matching constraint sets; review in Constraint Manager afterwards.

tools.name: .bsm / .osm / .ssm / .fsm (mechanical, format, shape and flash symbols)
tools.description: Compiled symbol types besides package symbols (.psm): mechanical symbols (.bsm) for board outlines, mounting holes and fixtures, format symbols (.osm) for drawing borders, shape symbols (.ssm) for custom pad shapes, and flash symbols (.fsm) for thermal-relief flashes on negative planes. Each is built from a .dra drawing and found through psmpath.
tools.usage: File > New > drawing type Mechanical symbol | Format symbol | Shape symbol | Flash symbol; File > Create Symbol
tools.example: Place > Manually > Advanced Settings > Library, then choose the MTG_HOLE_M3 mechanical symbol.
tools.notes: Upgrade old libraries with uprev_overwrite *.dra (and the compiled types) after a release change.
